root_cause.text: KVM’s x86 shadow MMU assumed that any present SPTE it encountered for a direct-mapped shadow page belonged to the expected GFN range (`sp->gfn + index`), so guest page-table changes could leave a leaf SPTE/rmap entry attached to a different GFN and later `rmap_remove()` would miss it, leaving a stale reverse-mapping to a freed `kvm_mmu_page`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `kvm_mmu_get_child_sp()` to only reuse a child shadow page when `spte_to_child_sp(*sptep)->gfn == gfn`, and in `__link_shadow_page()` it stops blindly dropping “large” SPTEs and instead zaps any existing present SPTE via `mmu_page_zap_pte()`; the CVE text explains the bug occurs because `rmap_remove()` only scans `[sp->gfn, sp->gfn + 511]` even though the recorded rmap can be outside that range after a guest write changes the mapping.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a forward declaration for `mmu_page_zap_pte` so it can be used before its definition.
intent_record.what: A new forward declaration was added for the function `mmu_page_zap_pte(struct kvm *kvm, struct kvm_mmu_page *sp, u64 *spte, struct list_head *invalid_list)` immediately after the existing declaration of `mmu_spte_set(u64 *sptep, u64 spte);`.
intent_record.how: This does not change runtime behavior by itself; it only makes the `mmu_page_zap_pte` function visible to code earlier in the file so it can be referenced before its definition, avoiding implicit-declaration or ordering issues.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unused drop_large_spte helper and fold its behavior into other SPTE handling paths.
intent_record.what: The static function drop_large_spte(struct kvm *kvm, u64 *sptep, bool flush) was removed entirely, including its local sp variable, the WARN_ON_ONCE check for PG_LEVEL_4K, the call to drop_spte(kvm, sptep), and the conditional kvm_flush_remote_tlbs_sptep(kvm, sptep) call.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this eliminates a dedicated helper that dropped a non-4K SPTE and optionally flushed remote TLBs; any code path that previously relied on this wrapper must now use other logic, with the same drop and flush behavior no longer encapsulated here.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix duplicate-child detection in kvm_mmu_get_child_sp() so -EEXIST is returned only when an existing child shadow page matches the requested gfn.
intent_record.what: The conditional in kvm_mmu_get_child_sp() was expanded: it now only returns -EEXIST when the shadow PTE is present, not large, and the existing child shadow page pointer from spte_to_child_sp(*sptep) is non-NULL and has a gfn matching the requested gfn. The old check only tested that the SPTE was present and not large.
intent_record.how: This change prevents treating any existing non-large shadow PTE as a duplicate child page unless it actually points to the same guest frame number. As a result, the function can create or select a child shadow page for a different gfn instead of incorrectly rejecting it with -EEXIST.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace large-SPTE dropping with explicit parent-page zapping and remote invalidation handling when installing a new shadow page.
intent_record.what: In __link_shadow_page(), the old single call to drop_large_spte(kvm, sptep, flush) inside the is_shadow_present_pte(*sptep) check was replaced with a block that derives parent_sp from sptep_to_sp(sptep), declares a local invalid_list, warns if parent_sp->role.level == PG_LEVEL_4K, zaps the PTE via mmu_page_zap_pte(kvm, parent_sp, sptep, &invalid_list), and then processes the invalidations with kvm_mmu_remote_flush_or_zap(kvm, &invalid_list, true).
intent_record.how: At runtime, present shadow PTEs are no longer removed through the old large-SPTE drop helper; instead, they are explicitly zapped through the parent shadow page and any resulting invalidations are flushed or zapped remotely. This makes the handling more precise for the parent MMU page, adds a runtime warning if the entry is unexpectedly at 4K level, and ensures stale mappings are invalidated through the invalidation list path.

Remove the unused drop_large_spte helper and fold its behavior into other SPTE handling paths.
Fix duplicate-child detection in kvm_mmu_get_child_sp() so -EEXIST is returned only when an existing child shadow page matches the requested gfn.
Replace large-SPTE dropping with explicit parent-page zapping and remote invalidation handling when installing a new shadow page.

relevance_review.reason: The change is only a forward declaration for a helper function and does not alter KVM shadow MMU/rmap handling, SPTE-GFN validation, or the stale reverse-mapping issue described in the root cause.

The change is a cleanup/refactor that removes an unused helper and folds its behavior into existing SPTE handling, but it does not address the shadow MMU reverse-mapping mismatch or the stale rmap issue described in the vulnerability root cause.

The change only fixes duplicate-child detection in kvm_mmu_get_child_sp() by checking that an existing child shadow page matches the requested GFN. The root cause is a stale reverse-mapping issue from mismatched SPTE/GFN assumptions in direct-mapped shadow pages and rmap_remove() missing entries, which is a different mechanism.

The change focuses on handling large SPTE replacement via parent-page zapping and remote invalidation when installing shadow pages, not on the root cause of stale reverse mappings caused by mismatched GFNs in direct-mapped shadow pages and missed rmap removal.

candidates.rationale: This assumption treats any already-present SPTE at the slot as something safe to drop/reuse when installing a new shadow page. The root cause is that a present SPTE could still be tied to a different GFN, so blindly handling it this way can leave stale reverse-mapping state attached to the freed shadow page.

This call embodies the vulnerable behavior of removing the existing SPTE without explicitly zapping the parent-page mapping for the correct GFN. Because the SPTE may not belong to the expected GFN range, reverse-mapping cleanup can miss it and leave a stale rmap entry.

This duplicate-child check assumes a present non-large SPTE is sufficient to conclude a duplicate child exists. The bug is about mismatched GFN ownership of an existing SPTE, so this kind of presence-based assumption can incorrectly bypass the need to validate the child against the requested GFN.

vuln_statements.explanation: This presence-based duplicate-child test can treat any existing non-large SPTE as the expected child without verifying that it matches the requested GFN, which is the core assumption that allows a mismatched leaf SPTE/rmap entry to persist.

This condition assumes any present SPTE in the slot is safe to handle as belonging to the intended shadow page, but the root cause is that a present SPTE may actually map a different GFN and later reverse-mapping cleanup can miss it.

This line performs the vulnerable removal path by dropping the existing SPTE without explicitly zapping the correct parent-page mapping for the owning GFN, which can leave stale rmap state attached to the freed shadow page.

commit 0cd8dc739833080aa0813cbd94d907a93e3a14c3
Author: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
Date:   Wed Jun 22 15:27:07 2022 -0400

    KVM: x86/mmu: pull call to drop_large_spte() into __link_shadow_page()
    
    Before allocating a child shadow page table, all callers check
    whether the parent already points to a huge page and, if so, they
    drop that SPTE.  This is done by drop_large_spte().
    
    However, dropping the large SPTE is really only necessary before the
    sp is install
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown diff already contains the fix for the root cause. The vulnerable condition was a present shadow SPTE that was treated as safe to overwrite/link without first dropping a large leaf and flushing, which could leave stale reverse mappings. In this version, `__link_shadow_page()` now explicitly handles that case: `if (is_shadow_present_pte(*sptep)) drop_large_spte(kvm, sptep);` and the comment says, `If an SPTE is present already, it must be a leaf and therefore a large one. Drop it and flush the TLB before installing sp.` Also, `kvm_mmu_get_child_sp()` now returns `ERR_PTR(-EEXIST)` when `is_shadow_present_pte(*sptep) && !is_large_pte(*sptep)`, preventing double-linking of an existing non-leaf. Because the fix is already present, the vulnerable construct is not present in this commit version.

The TLB flush before installing the newly-populated lower lev
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 0378739401cfc2fd2a50a2a337a4f394e8493008
Author: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
Date:   Wed Jun 22 15:27:10 2022 -0400

    KVM: x86/mmu: Avoid unnecessary flush on eager page split
    
    The TLB flush before installing the newly-populated lower level
    page table is unnecessary if the lower-level page table maps
    the huge page identically.  KVM knows it is if it did not reuse
    an existing shadow page table, tell drop_large_spte() to skip
    the flush in that case.
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body contains the split-page logic and the fix for the flush behavior, but not the vulnerable stale-rmap construct described in the root cause. In `shadow_mmu_split_huge_page()`, the code now tracks whether any existing SPTE is a non-leaf with `flush |= !is_last_spte(*sptep, sp->role.level);` and then passes that into `__link_shadow_page(kvm, cache, huge_sptep, sp, flush);`. The callee also conditionally flushes: `if (flush) kvm_flush_remote_tlbs_with_address(...)`. This is the corrected handling for partially populated lower-level page tables. The vulnerable issue was about a present SPTE/rmap entry attached to the wrong GFN and `rmap_remove()` missing it later, but this snippet only shows the flush-skip optimization and its safeguards; it does not show the faulty stale reverse-mapping condition itself. Therefore the vulnerable construct is absent here, and the fix is already present.
